line_or_sentence: l.56 (Type III paragraph), repeated at l.107; also sections/s03d_admiss.tex l.34 and sections/s17_open.tex l.95
manuscript_claim: GN-III has no finite propagation speed in the strict sense because the strongly damped wave equation smooths parabolically
what_source_says: Two different quantities are being compared. Green & Naghdi state (footnote 2, p.190) that both types II and III accommodate finite wave speed and only type II has no dissipation, meaning the intermediate-regime speed sqrt(k*/rho c). What the manuscript's own dispersion analysis shows is that the phase speed of GN-III is unbounded at high frequency, i.e. no sharp front. Both statements are correct about different objects; the word 'speed' carries the ambiguity, and the paragraph already concedes it in its last sentence without saying who claims otherwise
source_ref: Green & Naghdi 1993, J. Elasticity 31:189-208, footnote 2, p.190

manuscript_claim: the restrictions d alpha - h >= 0, h > 0 are 'Eqs. (4.14) and (4.16) of that paper'
what_source_says: The copy in the library yields text up to section 2 only; the abstract confirms the symmetric heat-conduction tensor and second-sound effects but not these inequalities. Equation numbers and the identifications tau_1 = alpha, tau_0 = h/d could not be checked
source_ref: Green & Lindsay 1972, p.1 abstract and sections 1-2 only

line_or_sentence: l.30 (synthesis table, Green-Lindsay row); same wording in sections/s03_foundations.tex l.73
manuscript_claim: tau_1 >= tau_0 > 0 is an 'entropy-inequality restriction, derived in Green1972'
what_source_says: The abstract does attribute the restrictions to an entropy-production inequality, so the provenance is right. The ordering itself was not visible in the part read, and sections/s03_foundations.tex l.73 itself notes that the original paper 'does not name a relaxation time' - so the tau names are the manuscript's relabelling, which this row understates

manuscript_claim: the classical coupled theory of Biot 'inherits the infinite thermal signal speed'
what_source_says: Consistent: the 1956 abstract ends from a variational/minimum-entropy-production formulation to the statement that 'the entropy density obeys a diffusion-type law', which is a parabolic, infinite-speed conduction law. No correction needed

line_or_sentence: l.12-31 (normal scattering and the Guyer-Krumhansl law)
manuscript_claim: the Guyer-Krumhansl law comes from the linearised phonon Boltzmann equation and gives a frequency-dependent conductivity
what_source_says: Consistent: the paper obtains 'a set of macroscopic equations which describe second sound with damping and Poiseuille flow' from a solution 'in terms of the eigenvectors of the normal-process collision operator', with a generalized conductivity sigma(k,Omega) that depends on wavenumber and frequency

manuscript_claim: MGT is the entry in the heat-law taxonomy
what_source_says: The source presents MGT as 'obtained after the introduction of a relaxation parameter in the Green-Naghdi type III model' and proves 3-D well-posedness/stability and 1-D exponential decay or instability depending on constitutive parameters. It gives no dispersion curve, so the 'wave-like at both ends' property asserted in the s06_lags.tex caption is the manuscript's own computation, not the source's

manuscript_claim: Quintanilla derived tau_T > tau_q/2 for the version with the flux expanded to second order in tau_q and the gradient to first order in tau_T
what_source_says: Accurate and correctly scoped: the paper states that solutions decay exponentially when t_gamma > t_q/2 and that unstable solutions exist when t_gamma < t_q/2, for exactly that truncation. Recorded so the sentence is not later widened to the whole DPL template
source_ref: J. Thermal Stresses 26(7):713-721, abstract and Eq. (1), p.713

manuscript_claim: Chen derives the ballistic-diffusive equations from the Boltzmann equation in the relaxation-time approximation
what_source_says: Accurate: the paper introduces 'new heat-conduction equations, named ballistic-diffusive equations, which are derived from the Boltzmann equation' under the relaxation-time approximation, Eq. (1)
source_ref: Phys. Rev. Lett. 86(11):2297 (2001), abstract and Eq. (1)

manuscript_claim: fitted speed about 3200 m/s at 85 K against 3650 m/s from ab initio calculations, oscillations at 104 and 125 K and none at 50 and 150 K
what_source_says: The abstract of the first-release version reports only that second sound was observed above 100 K in qualitative agreement with ab initio calculations; none of the four numbers is in it. The manuscript does flag them as first-release values without error bars, but they were not verified here
source_ref: Science, DOI 10.1126/science.aav3548, abstract of the 14 March 2019 first release

manuscript_claim: cited as the review of the heat-pulse experiments
what_source_says: Accurate: the paper presents the phonon extended thermodynamics as a unified theory and claims a full explanation of the heat-pulse experiments in which ballistic phonons, second sound and ordinary conduction compete

manuscript_claim: the Coleman-Noll procedure is the source of the entropy-inequality restrictions
what_source_says: Only the title page and section 1 were read: they set out the rational-thermodynamics programme and the entropy inequality as a restriction on constitutive functionals, which is consistent, but no theorem in the paper was checked
source_ref: Arch. Rational Mech. Anal. 13 (1963), title page and section 1 only
